item.title: How to reset MiniCycle and erase all your period records
item.description: Reset records wipes every period date, note, and activity mark in MiniCycle, and it cannot be undone. What it clears, what it keeps, and how to back up first.

item.title: How to start tracking your period: a beginner's guide
item.description: New to tracking? What to write down from day one, how a cycle is counted, why your first months of predictions stay rough, and the few changes worth a doctor's note.

item.title: Daily notes in MiniCycle: jot symptoms on any calendar day
item.description: Tap any date in MiniCycle to add a daily note: symptoms, flow, pain, mood, up to 999 characters. Notes stay on your device by default and never appear on the widget.

item.title: The fertile window: six days, and why apps estimate it
item.description: The fertile window is about six days: five before ovulation, one after. Why the window exists, and why any calendar estimate of it stays approximate.

item.title: MiniCycle in English: change the app language and dark mode
item.description: MiniCycle defaults to Korean. How to switch the app to English in two taps, choose System, Light, or Dark appearance, and what the home-screen widget follows.

item.title: Perimenopause period changes: what's normal and what's not
item.description: Cycles in perimenopause can shift by a week, skip months, or run heavier. Which period changes are expected before menopause, and which ones need a doctor.

item.title: Hide sexual activity in your period tracker with Face ID
item.description: MiniCycle logs sexual activity as a purple dot on the calendar. One switch hides every trace, and showing it again takes Face ID. What hiding does and doesn't do.

item.title: What counts as an irregular period, and when to see a doctor
item.description: Irregular periods usually have ordinary causes, but some patterns deserve a clinician. What counts as irregular, when to see a doctor, and how tracking actually helps.

item.title: Auto vs manual cycle and period length in MiniCycle
item.description: MiniCycle can estimate your cycle and period length, or let you set them by hand (21–42 and 1–10 days). When auto fits, when manual fits, and why the estimate uses a median.

item.title: What causes spotting between periods? Common reasons
item.description: Spotting between periods has many ordinary explanations, from ovulation to new birth control. Learn what is common, when to see a clinician, and how to track it.

item.title: Should a period calendar start on Sunday or Monday?
item.description: MiniCycle's calendar can start the week on Sunday or Monday. Why calendars disagree, why the choice changes only the layout, and how the widget stays in sync.

item.title: Ovulation signs and basal body temperature: the basics
item.description: Ovulation signs explained: the cervical fluid change before ovulation, the basal body temperature rise of about 0.3°C after it, and what ovulation tests show.

item.title: What each color means on the MiniCycle period calendar
item.description: What the MiniCycle calendar colors mean: solid pink records, striped expected periods, the sky-blue fertile window, and the small marks under each date.

item.title: What is a normal menstrual cycle length? It's a range
item.description: A normal menstrual cycle length is a range, not a single number. See the 24–38 day guideline, how much variation is common, and when to ask a clinician.

item.title: How to edit or fix a wrong period date in MiniCycle
item.description: Logged a period on the wrong day? Learn how to edit period dates in MiniCycle: move a start, adjust an end, delete a record, and what happens to predictions.

item.title: The menstrual cycle phases: follicular, ovulation, luteal
item.description: Learn the menstrual cycle phases: menstruation, the follicular phase, ovulation, and the luteal phase, what each one does, and why their lengths vary.

item.title: How to set up period and ovulation reminders in MiniCycle
item.description: MiniCycle can remind you 0–3 days before an expected period, the fertile window, or ovulation day. Learn how to set up period reminders and pick a time.

item.title: Why is my period late? Common non-pregnancy reasons
item.description: A late period has many non-pregnancy explanations, from stress to travel and illness. Learn common reasons a period can be late and when to ask a clinician.

item.title: How to keep your period tracker records when moving to a new iPhone
item.description: MiniCycle stores records locally by default and offers optional iCloud Sync. Learn what to check before moving to a new iPhone.

item.title: How MiniCycle estimates periods, ovulation, and the fertile window
item.description: Learn how MiniCycle estimates period dates, ovulation, and the fertile window using recent cycle records, median-based calculations, and published menstrual cycle research.

item.title: What a period calendar widget should show on the iPhone home screen
item.description: A practical guide to period calendar widgets, including glanceable cycle status, prediction labels, and why MiniCycle keeps its iPhone widget simple.

item.title: Private period tracking without an account: why MiniCycle stores records locally
item.description: MiniCycle keeps records local by default, offers optional iCloud Sync, and does not require a MiniCycle account.

item.title: Cycle length and period length: how to read simple period statistics
item.description: Understand cycle length, period length, recent averages, and why MiniCycle shows simple statistics instead of turning every cycle into a score.

item.title: When period tracker predictions are useful, and when they are not
item.description: Period tracker predictions can help with planning, but they are not medical advice, contraception, or a pregnancy test. Learn the limits MiniCycle makes explicit.
